main_body: Repeating brick wall-face pattern (stone bricks in running bond with dark mortar lines), a tileable terrain block
top_band: none. This is a flat tiling wall/paving texture, not a standing object. The column scan shows repeating brick courses: a light 1-row top highlight, 5 rows of mid-tone face, then 2 rows of shadow/mortar.
evidence: The kind is terrain (a wall-face autotile), so the standing-object top-band contract does not apply. Each brick has its own highlight on top and shadow below, which is the normal way to draw a wall face. There is no isometric side face and no top-down slab. Pass.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The paving reference has 7 and the grass reference has 26 colours per tile (80 colours in total). The 5 steps are a sensible ramp: highlight, mid, two shadow tones and a dark mortar tone. The brick faces are mostly one mid tone with only a few sparse speckle pixels, so grain is thin. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because of those scattered dots. The mortar and dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral (colour spread of 12 or less), so the outline reads as a neutral grey line, not a tinted material tone. The paving reference is at 80% neutral, so it is not clearly better there. Overall the piece is cleaner but thinner than the references, with low density and little per-brick shading variation. When in doubt, fail.
